title: Filling the GPU during decode
summary: Paged attention, continuous batching, prefix cache, and speculative decoding.

choices.text: Continuous batching waits until every sequence in the batch has finished, then admits a full new batch at once, so the GPU never runs a partly filled batch.
Prefix caching reuses the KV cache of a shared prompt prefix, such as a system prompt or a repeated document, across requests.
Speculative decoding serves the draft model's distribution. The target model is only a teacher used earlier, to distill the draft.

Speculative decoding lets a cheap draft propose several tokens, then checks them in one target forward pass. With the usual rejection correction, accepted tokens follow the target model's distribution.
Paged attention stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks and allocates them like virtual-memory pages, so a finished request's pages can be reused without a contiguous max-length buffer per request.
